source.title: UNDO (distillation)
source.authors: Bruce W. Lee; Addie Foote; Alex Infanger; Leni Shor; Harish Kamath; Jacob Goldman-Wetzler; B. Woodworth; Alex Cloud; Alexander Matt Turner

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether unlearned behavior returns under fine-tuning and quantization, and reports that ordinary unlearning is vulnerable while distillation-based methods improve resistance. This challenges and qualifies the general claim.
record.gate_note: The paper's relearning and quantization experiments bear directly on the claim. Figure-only relearning curves are recorded as figure-only rather than assigned values from the plots. Results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs forget-set relearning attacks (and, for TOFU, INT4 quantization) on GradDiff-, MaxEnt- and RMU-unlearned models, and on oracle-matched models. Unlearned-only models recover the forgotten capability. It then proposes distillation/UNDO as a counter-method and tests it against the same attacks. So its own results bear on versions A, B, D and F.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Authors conclude that standard unlearning, and even oracle matching, only suppresses behaviour, so a few fine-tuning steps recover it. Distilling into a fresh or noised student (UNDO) removes the latent capability. At its strongest setting UNDO matches data-filtering robustness on synthetic tasks with 60-80% of the compute. On WMDP it improves robustness but is only competitive with other methods and lowers MMLU by 4.88%.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes unlearning followed by distillation into a randomly initialized student or a noised copy (UNDO); it does not reproduce the original methods as its central intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Robustness changes with the unlearning method and domain; RMU distillation is less effective for arithmetic where its initial retain-forget trade-off is weaker. In UNDO, higher perturbation α generally improves resistance but requires more distillation compute; β has less impact in most tested settings. WMDP results are limited by the α setting, available distillation data, and retain-performance loss.
record.code_released: not stated (the text says code is shared publicly through GitHub but gives no URL)
record.problems: Many main relearning outcomes are shown only as figures, without values in the text. The WMDP setup uses only 0.015% of the stated Gemma-2-2B pretraining corpus for distillation, and the authors report a 4.88% average MMLU reduction. The paper's stated results for TOFU quantization apply to one model and one unlearning setup.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5 and Figure 6 contain additional UNDO perturbation and compute sweeps; Figure 7 and Figure 11 compare multiple methods and retain-forget trade-offs at several attack strengths. These were not separately catalogued because the record prioritizes direct relearning outcomes and the explicit quantization comparison. Appendix B.1 contains many learning-rate sweep outcomes for unlearning-only suppression; those do not report recovery attacks and are not itemized here.

untested.parts: Unrelated or loosely related relearning sets (all attacks use forget-domain data, often mixed with retain data).
Entirely untested. There is no activation-direction ablation or mechanistic analysis; the 'latent capability' reading rests only on fine-tuning recovery.
Methods other than GradDiff, models other than Gemma-2-2B, benchmarks other than TOFU, and precisions other than INT4.
UNDO is not tested against prompting or activation ablation. Quantization is tested only on TOFU with one model.

missing.what: Relearning curves for the unlearn-only MaxEnt and RMU baselines on WMDP-Bio/Cyber with Gemma-2-2B (best of seven adversaries)
Model utility under INT4: GradDiff 0.495 to 0.242, distilled 0.442 to 0.391
Pre-attack suppression levels showing near-chance forgetting with retain kept (e.g., MaxEnt arithmetic retain 0.795, forget 0.0125; RMU 62%/6.8%)

record.verdict_notes: The record's main errors: version C was linked from fine-tuning rows; distilled/UNDO rows were linked to A and B; and R10 was marked partial although it is unlearn-only. The study proposes UNDO, so its F evidence is the proposer's own. Relearning uses about 8M or 2M forget-domain tokens with a 10-learning-rate adversary, which is stronger than the 'small set' in B; the 40-step results in Figure 7 still show rapid degradation. The quantization test is a post-review appendix experiment on one model and one method. The reader-validation issue on labels[8] (R26 linked to F) is resolved: R26 now links to D only.

versions.untested_parts: Recovery attacks are tested, but near-chance suppression and preserved general ability are not jointly compared with an explicit chance level in every setting. Prompt-only attacks are not tested.
The paper tests fine-tuning on the forget data; it does not test unrelated or loosely related relearning examples.
No activation-direction ablation is tested. The paper's evidence concerns latent capabilities recovered through fine-tuning, rather than a direct internal edit.
Quantization is tested on the TOFU setup (Gemma-2-2B); other unlearning methods and benchmarks are not tested with this attack.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages as prompts, and in-context information are not tested as recovery attacks.
Distillation/UNDO is tested against fine-tuning and, in TOFU, quantization. It is not tested against activation-direction ablation or prompting-only attacks.

labels.reason: The text says SAM and RepNoise show significant performance deterioration under stronger relearning (Section 6, Fig 7).

relation.reason: Runs relearning and INT4 attacks on unlearned models.

tranche.reason: Shows that unlearn-only and oracle-matched models relearn quickly, and proposes a counter-method. T5 is acceptable.

source_check.notes: Most rows are figure-only; only Table 14 (TOFU INT4) gives numbers. The text says code is shared via GitHub (line 55), so the header's code: n and 'no code' in D.support[3] and F.support[2] are wrong. R20, R23 and R24 (cited by l5) are not in this pack. The 1.5B size for Phi-1.5 in R22 is not stated in the text.

statements.correction: GradDiff, MaxEnt and RMU unlearn-only: Gemma-2-0.1B (Korean) and Gemma-2-0.3B (arithmetic), 500 relearning steps. TOFU (Gemma-2-2B, Phi-1.5): GradDiff only, 100 relearning updates. Oracle: pretrained on retain data only (never on forget data). The oracle-matched reference relearns quickly (Fig 2).
statements.problem: The sentence reads as if GradDiff, MaxEnt and RMU were all run on TOFU. The TOFU runs used GradDiff only. Also, the 'never-trained oracle' was pretrained, just never on forget data.
Does not mention this study, so there is nothing to check.

statements.correction: NeurIPS 2025. Text p.1: 'We share our code implementation publicly through GitHub.' Uncertainty exists at study level (Fig 5: 5 seeds; Fig 8: 4 seeds), but Table 14's INT4 values come without uncertainty.
statements.problem: 0.000 to 0.185 and 'substantial' are right. 'No code' is contradicted: the text says the code is shared publicly through GitHub.
Numbers are right (0.000 to 0.008 Q&A prob; truth ratio 0.185). Minor: the bullet's 'challenges' label is stronger than this study's own verdict for this metric (l3 limits_scope).
Cites no rows. The Gemma-2-2B INT4 recovery shows on one setting and one metric (truth ratio).

statements.correction: Synthetic 0.1B/0.3B: distilled/UNDO relearning approaches the data-filtering curves in some cases, and RMU arithmetic is weaker. INT4 (Table 14): TOFU Gemma-2-2B GradDiff+Distilled (distilled onto the base model) forget truth ratio 0.001 to 0.017, against 0.185 for GradDiff alone. The text says code is shared through GitHub.
statements.problem: The INT4 truth ratio 0.017 is placed under the Gemma-2 0.1B/0.3B synthetic setting. It actually comes from the TOFU Gemma-2-2B GradDiff+Distilled model. 'No code' is contradicted by the text.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Oracle-matched reference models and unlearning-only GradDiff, MaxEnt, and RMU models under forget-data fine-tuning
reader_labels.reason: These models reacquire the forget behavior quickly after fine-tuning, contrary to the no-recovery part of the version (R1, R2, R5-R10).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Unlearn-and-Distill models in the tested language and arithmetic setups
reader_labels.reason: Distilled models are reported as more resistant to relearning, sometimes approaching the Data Filtering baseline, though exact values are not reported in the text (R11-R16).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Forget-set fine-tuning attacks on oracle-matched and unlearning-only models
reader_labels.reason: Fine-tuning on the forget data restores targeted performance quickly for these models (R1, R2, R5-R10, R21-R22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Unlearn-and-Distill models and TOFU models distilled onto a fresh base
reader_labels.reason: Distillation slows relearning substantially; TOFU trajectories are described as closer to never-exposed controls, and recovery is not reported as absent in all settings (R11-R16, R23-R24).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Unlearned models evaluated with forget-data fine-tuning
reader_labels.reason: Rapid recovery after behavioral suppression is evidence consistent with retained latent capability, although no activation-direction ablation is performed (R1-R2, R5-R10).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: TOFU Gemma-2-2B standard GradDiff-unlearned model under INT4 quantization
reader_labels.reason: Forget truth ratio increases from 0.000 to 0.185 after quantization (R26).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: TOFU Gemma-2-2B GradDiff-unlearned and distilled model under INT4 quantization
reader_labels.reason: The distilled model's forget truth ratio rises only from 0.001 to 0.017, and its Q&A probability rises from 0.000 to 0.003 (R27-R28).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Distillation/UNDO under fine-tuning relearning attacks in synthetic language, arithmetic, WMDP, and TOFU settings
reader_labels.reason: The authors report greater resistance than unlearning alone; TOFU results are closer to never-exposed controls, and WMDP UNDO improves resistance across tested configurations (R11-R24).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The distilled model has a smaller quantization-associated rise in forget truth ratio than standard GradDiff unlearning (R26, R28).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: UNDO is described as competitive rather than clearly superior on WMDP-Cyber, and its average MMLU performance is 4.88% lower (R17-R20).
